files.A/work/579.txt: Check whether a second van and driver can cover the east stop. If that’s still unconfirmed at the deadline, prioritize the west stop and notify the six east reservation holders of the delay. The detour takes 35 minutes, but the driver has only 25 minutes to spare. Serving west protects 18 reservations. Keep both stops if the second crew can cover east or a confirmed safe route brings the detour within the 25-minute margin.
files.A/work/143.txt: Recommend sending the bookmobile to the west stop only and telling the six east stop patrons now that their pickups will be rescheduled. With the low bridge closed, the detour takes 35 minutes and the driver has just 25 spare, so one vehicle can't cover both stops. West has 18 reservations to east's 6. I'd change course if the second van turns out to be available to cover east, or if the bridge reopens before departure.
files.A/work/802.txt: A bridge closure on today's bookmobile route is forcing a 35-minute detour, and the driver has only 25 minutes of slack in the schedule. This means the bookmobile will run at least 10 minutes behind, and the delay could affect either the west or east stop. We are checking whether a second van is available but do not know yet. Your reservation still stands. Please look for a follow-up message with confirmed times before heading to your stop.

files.A/work/249.txt:
Recommend splitting the queue now: keep gate 1 scanning and put one person at gate 2 checking tickets by eye, issuing paper tickets where needed. One working gate cannot clear 40 people in seven minutes, and a manual check is quicker than attempting a scanner fix.

If gate 2's scanner comes back, return to scanning there. If gate 1 also fails, go fully manual at both. If dispatch confirms a delayed departure, funnel everyone through gate 1 instead.
files.A/work/244.txt: Send the 40 waiting passengers through gate 1 now. If manual ticket checks are authorized, staff gate 2 and use paper tickets there rather than spend the seven minutes before departure troubleshooting the scanner. Check the boarding rate after one minute. If the remaining queue won’t clear in time, alert train control and ask whether the train can be held. If gate 2’s scanner comes back online, use both gates for scanning.
files.A/work/661.txt: The ticket scanner at Gate 2 is offline. Gate 1 is working, and about 40 people are in line. The regional train is due to depart in 7 minutes, so please head straight to Gate 1 and have your ticket ready. Paper tickets are available if you need one; ask a staff member where to get one. Please don’t wait at Gate 2.

files.A/work/729.txt: Before noon, ask the venue whether its 240 clicker count includes volunteers who used the side door and whether it counts reentries. If we can’t reconcile the counts by deadline, report 192 tickets scanned and attribute the 240 count to the venue; don’t present either as confirmed attendance. The figures may measure different things. I’d switch to a single attendance figure if the venue can document a count of unique attendees and clarify whether volunteers are included.
files.A/work/632.txt: Before noon, ask the venue what the clicker counted and the volunteer lead whether anyone tracked side-door entries. If the counts still conflict at deadline, report that the venue clicker recorded 240 and 192 tickets were scanned; don’t call either figure total attendance. Volunteers used the side door, but we don’t know whether that explains the gap. I’d use a single total if the entry records establish how many distinct people attended, including volunteers.
files.A/work/161.txt: Update on attendance for the local paper: we have two counts that don't match. The venue clicker recorded 240, but only 192 tickets were scanned. Volunteers came in through the side door, which may explain some of the 48-person gap, though we haven't confirmed that. The paper's deadline is noon. Please don't share either figure yet. If you worked the side door or know how many volunteers attended, reply with your numbers by 11 a.m.

files.A/work/208.txt: Before the lessons start, put the student who needs step-free access in the downstairs dry room, give the upstairs room to whichever lesson needs the piano, and move the third lesson online or reschedule it. Access is the one requirement we can't work around, so it has to be settled first. I'd change this if the step-free student is also the piano student (then bring a keyboard downstairs), or if the flooded room is cleared as safe in time.
files.A/work/982.txt: Before the deadline, keep the flooded room closed and confirm which dry room has a step-free route. Reserve that room for the student who needs it. If the upstairs room is the other dry room, use it for the piano lesson. Move the remaining lesson to the next available slot: two rooms can’t host three lessons at once. If a suitable third room becomes available in time, keep all three at their original time.
files.A/work/990.txt: One lesson room has flooded and is closed. We have two dry rooms for three lessons scheduled at the same time, so one lesson will need to move to a different time. We’re reserving the step-free room for the student who needs it; the other available room is upstairs and has a piano. Please stay clear of the flooded room and check your messages for your room assignment or a new lesson time before heading in.

files.A/work/887.txt: Before the deadline, confirm the first, paid booking and contact the second party to offer a reschedule with the instructor. The instructor booking doesn’t justify bumping the first crew, and easing wind doesn’t make the spare safe while its mast inspection is incomplete. I’d keep both bookings if the spare passes inspection before launch and conditions are within club limits. If the first crew cancels, offer their dinghy to the instructor-led group.
files.A/work/133.txt: Before the deadline, confirm the first paid booking for the dinghy. Tell the instructor and the second group about the clash and offer them the next available slot. The instructor’s presence and the easing wind don’t establish that the spare mast is safe. Keep the spare ashore unless it passes inspection. If it’s cleared in time and conditions are suitable, run both bookings; if the first group cancels, offer its dinghy to the second group.
files.A/work/755.txt: Two bookings were accepted for the same dinghy in the same slot. The first booking is paid, and the second includes an instructor. Our spare boat cannot be used yet because its mast inspection is not finished, so only one boat is confirmed. The wind is easing, so the session itself can still go ahead. Please do not rig or launch for now. Both parties should come to the club office so we can agree who sails and rearrange the other booking.

files.B/work/366.txt:
Grab the spare probe from the front desk and take a third reading in the shallow end before lessons start in 20 minutes. The fixed sensor shows 25 °C and the handheld 28 °C, a gap too wide to trust either one, so log whichever value the spare confirms.

If the spare matches neither, or the confirmed temperature falls outside our allowed range for lessons, hold the class and flag it to maintenance instead of starting on time.
files.B/work/116.txt: Get the spare probe from the front desk now and complete the staff check before lessons start in 20 minutes. Take all three readings at the same spot and depth in the shallow end; the current 25 °C and 28 °C readings don’t tell us which is reliable. If the spare is calibration-verified and confirms a temperature within the lesson range, record the result and proceed. Otherwise, delay lessons until you can verify the temperature.
files.B/work/553.txt: The shallow-end sensor reads 25 °C, but a handheld thermometer reads 28 °C, so the water temperature is not yet confirmed. Lessons are scheduled to start in 20 minutes. Staff will use the spare probe at the front desk to check the temperature before lessons. Please stay out of the pool until staff confirm whether lessons can start as scheduled.

files.B/work/403.txt: Fire the 16 labelled tests tonight, each in the kiln that matches its stated temperature, and hold back the two unlabelled glazes. Guessing risks underfiring them in kiln A or, worse, overfiring in kiln B, where a low-temperature glaze could run and damage shelves and neighbouring pieces. Two late tests cost less than a ruined load. If someone confirms their firing temperatures from the maker, supplier, or batch notes before loading, include them in the right kiln.
files.B/work/764.txt: Before tonight’s firing, set aside the two unlabeled glaze tests. Check each of the other 16 against its recommended firing range, group tests with compatible ranges, and choose a firing temperature within that range. Use kiln A if it can reach the chosen temperature; use kiln B for temperatures above 1180°C and up to 1240°C. An unknown glaze could run and damage a shelf. Add either held test only if reliable firing instructions confirm it fits a scheduled load.
files.B/work/236.txt: Tonight’s firing is scheduled for 18 glaze tests. Kiln A reaches 1180°C and kiln B reaches 1240°C. Two tests are missing firing-temperature labels and will be held out unless their required temperatures can be confirmed before loading. Please check your test labels before tonight’s firing. If one is yours, send the studio its glaze name and confirmed firing temperature. If you’re unsure of the temperature, leave the test out of both kilns.

files.B/work/132.txt: Before learners arrive, take the extractor out of service and move the class to the spare room for hand-tool work that doesn’t generate airborne dust. Don’t reset the outlet again or run dust-producing machines without extraction. Two shutdowns and a startup trip despite a fresh filter point to an unresolved equipment or electrical fault. Resume the planned session only after a qualified technician clears the extractor and circuit and confirms reliable extraction under load.
files.B/work/258.txt: Before learners arrive, move the class to the spare room and plan hand-tool work that doesn’t require extraction. Unplug the extractor, mark it out of use, and leave the outlet tripped. Two shutdowns despite a fresh filter, plus the outlet tripping on startup, warrant an electrical check rather than another reset. Resume powered work only after a qualified person checks the extractor and circuit and confirms the extractor starts, runs, and collects dust safely.
files.B/work/867.txt: Update for today's woodworking class: the dust extractor has shut down twice, and after we fitted a fresh filter the outlet now trips whenever it starts up. The cause isn't known yet, so the machines are off limits until it's checked. Class is still going ahead. Please go straight to the spare room when you arrive, where we'll work with hand tools instead. Don't switch on the extractor or reset the outlet yourself.

files.B/work/856.txt:
Recommend we run "more than 190 attended," citing the 192 scanned tickets, and add that the venue's own count was 240. The ticket figure is the only verifiable one, and the gap is probably volunteers who came in through the side door, but nobody has confirmed that.

If the organizer confirms about 48 volunteers before noon, switch to 240 total. If the clicker was only at the main door, the gap is unexplained, so drop the 240 entirely.
files.B/work/437.txt: Before noon, ask the venue what the clicker counted and the volunteer lead whether anyone tracked side-door entries. If the counts still conflict at deadline, report that the venue clicker recorded 240 and 192 tickets were scanned; don’t call either figure total attendance. Volunteers used the side door, but we don’t know whether that explains the gap. I’d use a single total if the entry records establish how many distinct people attended, including volunteers.
files.B/work/263.txt: We’re checking two attendance figures before the local paper’s noon deadline: the venue clicker recorded 240 entries, while 192 tickets were scanned. Volunteers used the side door, but we don’t yet know whether that accounts for the difference. If you staffed an entrance or kept a separate tally, please send your count and note whether volunteers were included before noon. Until we verify the numbers, please don’t share either figure as the final attendance count.

files.B/work/259.txt: Update on the lantern parade: showers are forecast, and that's a problem for our 30 paper lanterns. The route guide is already printed and stands unless you hear otherwise. For now, keep your lantern somewhere dry and watch for our message by 5.

files.A/work/514.txt: Fire the 16 labelled tests tonight, each in the kiln that matches its stated temperature, and hold back the two unlabelled glazes. Guessing risks underfiring them in kiln A or, worse, overfiring in kiln B, where a low-temperature glaze could run and damage shelves and neighbouring pieces. Two late tests cost less than a ruined load. If someone confirms their firing temperatures from the maker, supplier, or batch notes before loading, include them in the right kiln.
files.A/work/561.txt: Before tonight’s firing, set aside the two unlabeled glaze tests. Check each of the other 16 against its recommended firing range, group tests with compatible ranges, and choose a firing temperature within that range. Use kiln A if it can reach the chosen temperature; use kiln B for temperatures above 1180°C and up to 1240°C. An unknown glaze could run and damage a shelf. Add either held test only if reliable firing instructions confirm it fits a scheduled load.
files.A/work/922.txt: Tonight’s firing is scheduled for 18 glaze tests. Kiln A reaches 1180°C and kiln B reaches 1240°C. Two tests are missing firing-temperature labels and will be held out unless their required temperatures can be confirmed before loading. Please check your test labels before tonight’s firing. If one is yours, send the studio its glaze name and confirmed firing temperature. If you’re unsure of the temperature, leave the test out of both kilns.

Leave the accessible manual shutoff to staff, since closing it would also stop water to the fountain.

files.B/work/934.txt: Move today's class into the spare room and run it as a hand-tool session; keep the extractor unplugged and tagged out before learners arrive. files.B/work/883.txt: Before learners arrive, move the class to the spare room and plan hand-tool work that doesn’t require extraction. Resume powered work only after a qualified person checks the extractor and circuit and confirms the extractor starts, runs, and collects dust safely.
files.B/work/569.txt: Today’s woodworking class will start in the spare room with hand-tool activities. Do not reset the outlet, restart the extractor, or use the workshop’s power tools until the equipment and outlet have been checked.

files.B/work/445.txt: Tonight’s firing is scheduled for 18 glaze tests. Kiln A reaches 1180°C and kiln B reaches 1240°C.
